# v0.24.1 — #488: replay skips are bound to proven emitted occurrences; #517 rollback-readable proof

Qualified at the release candidate tag `v0.24.1-rc1` (`df5e2f14`): this GA tree is that tree plus this file
(RELEASE-READINESS-V1; `git diff --name-status v0.24.1-rc1..v0.24.1` = only this file).

Patch release on top of `v0.24.0` (`d346ab9e`). Runtime change: the compaction commit proof now records
per-emission descriptors, and every consumer that may skip a replayed row consults that projection
instead of the row's shape. No default, config key, tool or privacy posture changed; the only logging change is one
new DEBUG line (the emission-descriptor count at each compaction) — `LCM plugin loaded` and every `lcm_*` name are unchanged.
The durable commit proof keeps the version-3 wire format and carries the emission descriptors under
`descriptor_version: 4` (#517), so v0.24.0 still reads it after a rollback; version-2 and version-3 proofs
from earlier releases are still honoured for exact cursor matching (they never authorize a skip on their own).

## Changes since v0.24.0 (#488: #510 emission descriptors, #515 consumer switch; #517 rollback-readable proof)

`v0.24.0` shipped #488 as a known limitation: a user row that exactly copied the session's own summary
block (or an objective head, or a host-merged summary + new text) could be classified as replayed
scaffolding by its shape and skipped, so an authored row was never stored. The fix lands in two steps.

- #510 (additive): when a compaction emits a summary carrier, a standalone summary or an objective head,
  the commit proof records a descriptor for that emission — kind, role, the generated span digest and
  length, the bound row's current suffix witness (digest + length), the same-prefix ordinal in the
  complete list, the output multiplicity and, for a folded carrier, the retained source. A pure
  projection (`_project_emitted_occurrences`) maps a later message list onto those descriptors:
  a row projects as an emitted occurrence only when its role, prefix, suffix witness and ordinal all
  match; a prefix extension (Hermes merge-append) projects the remainder; everything else declines.
  Carry-forward re-binds the witness to the current carrier suffix on every compaction; a malformed
  durable proof never blocks a fresh proof.
- #515 (the switch): every replay skip is now occurrence-bound. The ingest store-tail walk, the durable
  proof restart walk, the in-order store-id mapper, the retained anchor, the replay cache and the
  head-rewrite comparisons take their identities from the projection of the COMPLETE list (subset
  callers slice one shared projection). A row the projection declines keeps its full identity and is
  stored — the store direction. A row the host merged into an emitted one (#499 composite) maps to,
  and replays as, its own stored whole row. With no version-4 proof in force (never compacted, or a
  version-2/3 proof from an earlier release), the replay path keeps its v0.24.0 shape until the session's
  first version-4 compaction ("legacy-proof window"): earlier proofs carry no digest for the emitted head,
  so exact cursor matching still relies on the v0.24.0 scaffold rules there, narrowed so that an objective
  head with new text merged behind it is stored whole. Malformed descriptors are declined, never raised on.
- #517 (#518, found by the Phase B rollback item of this release's gauntlet): #510 had written the durable proof as
  top-level version 4, which v0.24.0 ignores; a rollback to v0.24.0 after a v0.24.1 compaction then re-stored the
  last compaction's rows on the proof-less restart, and the next v0.24.0 compaction hit
  `publication_invariant_conflict` (that conversation could no longer compact on v0.24.0; no loss). Measured to
  be v0.24.0's own proof-less-restart class (deleting the proof on v0.24.0 itself reproduces it). The durable
  record now stays version 3 on the wire — `effective_sha256`/`scaffold_sha256` computed exactly as v0.24.0
  computes them — and carries the descriptors, the projected digest lists and the reset binding under
  `descriptor_version: 4`; this release's reader relabels a bound record to version 4 in memory and swaps the
  projected lists in, so every downstream version-4 predicate is untouched; an unbound top-level version-4
  record (unreleased main only) is treated as no proof.
- Measured (reviewer probes, both hosts; #515 merge receipt): 0 worse-lost and 0 worse-freeze cells versus v0.24.0 across
  the reviewer probe set; 80 tail-0 prefix/restart cells move from a lost row in v0.24.0 to one stored duplicate (accepted,
  disclosed in #515); the other probe cells improve or stay equal (per-probe breakdown in the #515 merge receipt and its
  comparator outputs).

Accepted direction: what a shape rule used to skip is now stored, so a byte-identical re-paste of the
session's own summary or objective is stored as an authored row (one bounded duplicate of generated text,
#501 class), and at tail 0 the Hermes todo snapshot merged into an emitted objective head is stored once
after a restart. Authored bytes are never dropped by shape once a version-4 proof is in force; inside the legacy-proof window
the v0.24.0 residual (an authored row equal to the session's own summary block, or a summary prefix glued
to text that is already stored) is unchanged and pinned by a strict xfail.

## Known follow-ups and limitations (tracked)

- #516 — replay identity truncates everything after the Hermes todo annotation; a user row the host
  merges behind it is not stored (pre-existing, unchanged here).
- #513 — `LCM_TEST_HERMES_AGENT_ROOT` opt-in leaks the real host import into later test modules
  (test-order only; no runtime effect).
- #514 — harden prior-proof consumption against malformed nested descriptor shapes beyond the checks
  fixed here (load-time validation of `output`, `of` against the output's cardinality, corrupted integers;
  carry only the projection entries the occurrence-level pass still binds; the same-byte attribution limit:
  among several stored candidates with identical bytes above the frontier the earliest is chosen).
- #499 residual — the objective-head merge at tail 0 in place no longer loses the merged row; the
  post-restart duplicate of generated text is the accepted direction above.
- #506, #507, #509 — proactive-recall carrier adjacency, rotation carry follow-ups, native summary
  re-attempt holds (unchanged from v0.24.0).
- #519: in the in-process rollback proof, a synthetic rotation into an empty child followed by a restart before the
  first child row makes the child's next compaction fail its publication invariant (freeze direction, no loss) on
  v0.24.0 and v0.24.1 alike (differential D1–D5); the live rotation cell of the v0.24.0 gauntlet did not show it;
  to be settled with one live `in_place: false` cell that restarts right after a rotation. In-place (default) is untouched.

## Benchmark boundary

No benchmark or scoring path changed. The proof format change adds bounded work to replay reconciliation:
a per-compaction occurrence projection, plus set-membership checks on ingest and store-tail mapping that are
linear in the replayed list (gpt-6-astra sweep B-PERF-1, P3). Assembly, summarization, recall and the doctor
scans are untouched. v0.24.0 numbers stand.

## Upgrade

`hermes plugins update hermes-lcm-x` (or reinstall at the tag). No config change from v0.24.0. Upgrading straight from
v0.23.x (`hermes-lcm`): do the v0.24.0 migration first — one installed LCM copy, `plugins.enabled` `hermes-lcm` →
`hermes-lcm-x` and `context.engine: lcm-x`, changed while Hermes is stopped (README, "Migrating from hermes-lcm"). The first compaction
after the upgrade writes a version-3 proof that carries `descriptor_version: 4`; earlier proofs are read for exact
cursor matching only.
Rollback to v0.24.0 is a plain reinstall: the durable proof stays readable by v0.24.0, so the restart after a
rollback re-stores nothing and that conversation keeps compacting (measured on the merged candidate: 0
rows re-stored, next v0.24.0 compaction committed with a plain version-3 proof); re-upgrading later is equally clean
(a legacy-proof window until the next v0.24.1 compaction). Residual (#517 R1, native recovery only — off on every
qualified host): after a rollback, a native-recovery record can still re-store a host-dropped orphan tool row on rare
shapes (duplicate direction, no loss).
